title: True or False: The Scrum Master is responsible for creating the Definition of Done for the team. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team is collectively responsible for creating the Definition of Done, with the Scrum Master facilitating the process. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is created collaboratively by the Scrum Team, not solely by the Scrum Master.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Team collectively defines the Definition of Done, with the Scrum Master facilitating the process.

title: True or False: The Definition of Done is used to establish the minimum quality standard that each Increment must meet before it is considered complete. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done sets the minimum quality standards for each Increment, ensuring that all completed work meets the agreed criteria. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Definition of Done ensures that each Increment meets the agreed-upon quality standards and is usable.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Definition of Done defines the criteria that each Increment must meet to be considered complete.

title: Which three pillars of Scrum help ensure continuous improvement within the team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The three pillars of Scrum—Transparency, Inspection, and Adaptation—are essential to ensuring continuous improvement, allowing the team to inspect and adapt their work processes regularly. These pillars are critical to Scrum’s success. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Transparency
explanation1: Correct: Transparency ensures that every aspect of the process is visible to those responsible, enabling informed decisions.
answer2: Commitment
explanation2: Incorrect: Commitment is a value, not a pillar, and does not directly ensure continuous improvement.
answer3: Inspection
explanation3: Correct: Inspection allows the team to regularly check their work and processes, identifying areas for improvement.
answer4: Adaptation
explanation4: Correct: Adaptation enables the team to make adjustments to their process based on what they learn from inspections.
answer5: Respect
explanation5: Incorrect: Respect is a value, not a pillar, though it supports a healthy team environment.

title: How should the Scrum Master handle a situation where the Developers frequently miss deadlines? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate the Sprint Retrospective to help the team identify why they are missing deadlines and collaboratively create a plan to improve. The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements to be enacted during the next Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Extend the deadlines to give the team more time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Extending deadlines undermines the time-boxing principles of Scrum.
answer2: Facilitate a Retrospective to help the team identify root causes and create an improvement plan.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective is an opportunity for the team to reflect on missed deadlines and make plans to improve future performance.
answer3: Report the issue to management for intervention.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should help the team improve their process internally, not escalate to management.
answer4: Assign new tasks to different team members to ensure they are completed on time.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Developers are self-managing and should decide how to organize their own work.

title: During a Sprint, the Product Owner requests changes to the Sprint Backlog that could impact the Sprint Goal. How should the Scrum Team respond? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team should evaluate the impact of the requested changes on the Sprint Goal, making collaborative decisions to maintain focus and alignment with the Sprint objectives. The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint, providing guidance to the Developers on why they are building the Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Implement the changes immediately to accommodate the Product Owner’s request.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes that impact the Sprint Goal should be carefully evaluated and not made impulsively.
answer2: Discuss the requested changes with the Scrum Team to assess their impact on the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: The team should evaluate the impact of the changes collaboratively before making any decisions.
answer3: Ignore the request and focus on the current Sprint Backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: The team should consider feedback but ensure changes do not compromise the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Extend the Sprint duration to accommodate the changes.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed and should not be extended.

title: A Developer suggests using a new tool that could improve the team's workflow. What is the best approach for the Scrum Team? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Retrospective is the right place to discuss potential workflow improvements, allowing the team to collectively decide on adopting new tools or processes. The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint. It is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements to be enacted during the next Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Implement the tool immediately to take advantage of its benefits.
explanation1: Incorrect: Any changes to the workflow should be discussed and agreed upon by the team.
answer2: Discuss the tool in the next Sprint Retrospective to decide if it should be adopted.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective is the best time to discuss potential improvements and decide on changes to the team's workflow.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to decide if the tool should be used.
explanation3: Incorrect: The decision should be made collaboratively by the team, not dictated by the Scrum Master.
answer4: Ignore the suggestion to avoid disrupting the current process.
explanation4: Incorrect: Improvements should be considered to enhance team effectiveness.

title: Which three strategies can help a Scrum Team maintain a sustainable pace? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maintaining a sustainable pace involves setting realistic Sprint Goals, inspecting and adapting through Retrospectives, and prioritizing high-value work, ensuring the team can continue delivering effectively. The Scrum framework is grounded in empiricism and lean thinking, emphasizing continuous improvement. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Setting realistic Sprint Goals that reflect the team’s capacity.
explanation1: Correct: Realistic Sprint Goals help the team maintain a sustainable pace and avoid overcommitment.
answer2: Extending work hours during busy periods.
explanation2: Incorrect: Overworking can lead to burnout and does not align with maintaining a sustainable pace.
answer3: Inspecting and adapting during Retrospectives to improve workflow.
explanation3: Correct: Retrospectives help the team continuously improve their process and pace.
answer4: Prioritizing high-value work to focus on what matters most.
explanation4: Correct: Focusing on high-value items ensures the team delivers meaningful work without unnecessary strain.
answer5: Skipping Daily Scrums to save time.
explanation5: Incorrect: Daily Scrums are essential for team alignment and should not be skipped.

title: How should the Scrum Master handle repeated conflicts between Developers during the Daily Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate a separate discussion to address conflicts among Developers, ensuring that the Daily Scrum remains focused and productive. The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team in several ways, including facilitating Scrum events as requested or needed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allow the conflicts to continue to see if the team resolves them independently.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should intervene to facilitate conflict resolution when it disrupts team dynamics.
answer2: Facilitate a separate discussion outside of the Daily Scrum to address the conflicts.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions outside of the Daily Scrum to resolve conflicts without disrupting the event.
answer3: Report the conflicts to management for resolution.
explanation3: Incorrect: Conflicts should be managed within the team, with the Scrum Master’s facilitation, not escalated externally.
answer4: Assign roles to team members to prevent further conflicts.
explanation4: Incorrect: The team should self-organize, and roles should not be imposed by the Scrum Master.

title: The Product Owner is often unavailable during important Scrum events, causing delays in decision-making. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach the Product Owner on their role and the importance of being available for key Scrum events, ensuring effective collaboration and decision-making. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team understand the need for clear and concise Product Backlog items. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Take over the Product Owner’s responsibilities during their absence.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not take over other roles but supports them in fulfilling their responsibilities.
answer2: Coach the Product Owner on the importance of attending Scrum events and engaging with the team.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should coach the Product Owner to ensure they understand their role in Scrum events and decision-making.
answer3: Allow the team to proceed without the Product Owner’s input.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s input is essential for guiding the work and making informed decisions.
answer4: Adjust the event schedule to accommodate the Product Owner’s availability.
explanation4: Incorrect: Events should be consistent and predictable, not adjusted ad hoc to fit individual schedules.

title: Which two strategies can help a Scrum Team maintain focus during the Daily Scrum? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Encouraging concise updates and using a rotating facilitator help the Scrum Team maintain focus and engagement during the Daily Scrum. The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allowing each team member unlimited time to share their updates.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum should be time-boxed to 15 minutes to maintain focus and efficiency.
answer2: Encouraging concise updates focused on progress toward the Sprint Goal, impediments, and plans for the next 24 hours.
explanation2: Correct: Keeping updates concise helps the team stay focused on the key aspects of the Daily Scrum.
answer3: Using a rotating facilitator to keep the team engaged and on track during the meeting.
explanation3: Correct: A rotating facilitator can bring variety and maintain engagement while keeping the meeting structured.
answer4: Skipping the Daily Scrum on days when there are no critical updates.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum should be held consistently to maintain alignment and communication.
answer5: Focusing discussions solely on individual performance rather than team progress.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum should focus on team progress and how to achieve the Sprint Goal, not individual performance.

title: The Scrum Master notices that the team’s velocity has decreased over the last few Sprints. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate a Retrospective to help the team identify the causes of decreased velocity and plan improvements, fostering continuous growth and adaptation. The Scrum Team continuously improves, adjusting its practices based on inspection and adaptation. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ignore the decrease as long as the Sprint Goals are being met.
explanation1: Incorrect: A decreasing velocity can indicate deeper issues that should be inspected and addressed.
answer2: Facilitate a Retrospective focused on identifying the causes of decreased velocity and potential improvements.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective is the right event to inspect performance and adapt the team’s practices.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to add fewer items to the Sprint Backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Developers and Scrum Team collaboratively decide on the Sprint Backlog based on capacity.
answer4: Report the issue to stakeholders and request additional resources.
explanation4: Incorrect: Velocity concerns should be managed within the Scrum Team, not escalated externally.

title: How can the Scrum Team ensure that the Definition of Done is consistently met? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team should regularly inspect and adapt the Definition of Done during Retrospectives, ensuring it aligns with the team's capabilities and maintains the required quality standards. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed as part of the Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Lower the Definition of Done when work is too challenging to meet it.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering the standards compromises the quality of the Increment and does not align with Scrum values.
answer2: Regularly review and update the Definition of Done during Retrospectives to align with team capabilities.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective is a key opportunity to inspect and adapt the Definition of Done, ensuring it remains relevant and achievable.
answer3: Only apply the Definition of Done to items that are easy to complete.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Definition of Done must be consistently applied to all work, regardless of difficulty.
answer4: Allow the Product Owner to decide when the Definition of Done applies.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is agreed upon by the entire Scrum Team and should be consistently applied.

title: Which Scrum value is demonstrated when a team member volunteers to help a colleague complete their tasks? (Choose the best answer)
answer1: Respect
explanation1: Incorrect: Respect involves valuing each other's contributions but is not specifically about helping with tasks.
answer2: Commitment
explanation2: Incorrect: Commitment involves dedication to the team’s goals but does not directly address helping others.
answer3: Courage
explanation3: Incorrect: Courage is about taking risks and facing challenges, not specifically about collaboration.
answer4: Focus
explanation4: Incorrect: Focus relates to concentrating on the Sprint Goal but not specifically about teamwork.
answer5: Openness
explanation5: Correct: Openness is demonstrated when team members share work and help each other to achieve the team’s goals.

title: The Scrum Team has identified that their Sprint Review sessions often lack stakeholder engagement. What can they do to improve this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Facilitating more interactive Sprint Reviews can improve stakeholder engagement, encouraging active participation and valuable feedback that guides future work. The Sprint Review is a working session, and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Skip the Sprint Review if stakeholders are not engaged.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is a critical event for inspection and adaptation, and should not be skipped.
answer2: Facilitate more interactive Sprint Reviews to encourage stakeholder participation and feedback.
explanation2: Correct: Making the Sprint Review more engaging can encourage stakeholders to actively participate and provide valuable feedback.
answer3: Invite stakeholders only when major changes are being presented.
explanation3: Incorrect: Stakeholders should be involved regularly to stay informed and engaged with the product’s progress.
answer4: Provide detailed reports instead of holding a Sprint Review.
explanation4: Incorrect: Direct engagement during the Sprint Review is more effective than reports for gaining feedback and adapting.

title: During the Sprint Planning, the Product Owner is unable to attend. What should the Scrum Team do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Planning should involve the Product Owner to set the Sprint Goal and prioritize work; rescheduling ensures their essential input is included. The Product Owner ensures that attendees are prepared to discuss the most important Product Backlog items and how they map to the Product Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Proceed with the planning without the Product Owner.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s presence is crucial for prioritization and setting the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Reschedule the Sprint Planning to ensure the Product Owner can participate.
explanation2: Correct: Rescheduling ensures that the Product Owner can provide necessary input on the Sprint Goal and selected items.
answer3: Continue planning and ask the Scrum Master to represent the Product Owner’s interests.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not represent the Product Owner’s decision-making responsibilities.
answer4: Replace the Product Owner with a stakeholder for this meeting.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s unique role cannot be substituted by a stakeholder.

title: A Developer repeatedly works on tasks outside of the Sprint Backlog. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate a discussion to reinforce the importance of adhering to the Sprint Backlog, ensuring the team remains focused on the Sprint Goal. The Sprint Backlog is a highly visible, real-time picture of the work that the Developers plan to accomplish during the Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Developer to complete their current task and refocus on the Sprint Backlog items.
explanation1: Incorrect: While this addresses the immediate issue, it does not prevent recurrence or address the root cause.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the team to reinforce the importance of adhering to the Sprint Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: A team discussion will help align the Developers on the importance of sticking to the agreed plan to achieve the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Ignore the issue if the additional work seems beneficial.
explanation3: Incorrect: Any work outside the Sprint Backlog distracts from the Sprint Goal and should not be ignored.
answer4: Assign additional tasks from the Sprint Backlog to the Developer to keep them busy.
explanation4: Incorrect: Assigning tasks does not address the issue of deviating from planned work.

title: Which three actions can help a Scrum Team improve their Definition of Done? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Improving the Definition of Done involves regular reviews during Retrospectives, incorporating stakeholder feedback, and ensuring team collaboration, which helps maintain high-quality Increments. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed as part of the Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Review the Definition of Done regularly during Sprint Retrospectives.
explanation1: Correct: Regular reviews during Retrospectives help ensure the Definition of Done remains relevant and achievable.
answer2: Allow the Product Owner to define the Definition of Done independently.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Definition of Done should be a shared agreement among the entire Scrum Team.
answer3: Incorporate feedback from stakeholders on quality expectations.
explanation3: Correct: Stakeholder feedback ensures the Definition of Done aligns with external quality standards and expectations.
answer4: Simplify the Definition of Done to speed up the completion of tasks.
explanation4: Incorrect: Simplifying may compromise the quality of the work delivered.
answer5: Collaborate with the entire Scrum Team to agree on updates to the Definition of Done.
explanation5: Correct: Collaborative updates ensure that all team members are aligned with the standards of completeness.

title: How should a Scrum Team handle a situation where they consistently overestimate their capacity during Sprint Planning? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Retrospective allows the Scrum Team to inspect their estimation and capacity planning, enabling them to make necessary adjustments to improve future Sprints. The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements to be enacted during the next Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Increase their work hours to complete the additional tasks.
explanation1: Incorrect: Overworking is not sustainable and does not address the underlying estimation issues.
answer2: Use the Retrospective to inspect and adjust their estimation techniques and capacity planning.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective is the appropriate place for the team to reflect on and improve their estimation practices.
answer3: Reduce the Sprint Goal to match what they are able to complete.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal should be realistic from the start and not adjusted mid-Sprint.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the team’s workload during the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Developers are responsible for managing their own workload and planning.

title: Which Scrum artifact provides visibility into the progress toward the Product Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog provides visibility into the progress toward the Product Goal by containing all items needed for the product's evolution, ordered by priority. The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: The Sprint Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog provides visibility into the current Sprint, not the overall Product Goal.
answer2: The Product Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Product Backlog includes all items necessary to achieve the Product Goal, providing visibility into overall progress.
answer3: The Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment shows completed work but does not provide a full view of progress toward the Product Goal.
answer4: The Definition of Done
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not track progress toward the Product Goal.

title: How can the Scrum Master support the Developers in maintaining high quality in their work? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master facilitates adherence to the Definition of Done and encourages continuous improvement, helping the Developers maintain high quality in their work. The Scrum Master serves the Developers by coaching them in self-management and cross-functionality. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Inspect the work completed and provide feedback regularly.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not inspect or judge the quality of the Developers’ work.
answer2: Facilitate the team’s adherence to the Definition of Done and encourage continuous improvement.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master supports quality by helping the team adhere to the Definition of Done and fostering an environment of continuous improvement.
answer3: Assign tasks based on the team members’ strengths to ensure high-quality outcomes.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Developers are self-managing and should decide how to organize their work.
answer4: Take over quality control to ensure standards are met.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Developers are responsible for meeting quality standards, not the Scrum Master.

title: Which two responsibilities belong to the Product Owner regarding the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner is responsible for ensuring the Product Backlog is visible, transparent, and ordered to maximize value, guiding the Scrum Team’s work. The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog, including its content, availability, and ordering. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ensuring the Product Backlog is visible and transparent to all stakeholders.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner makes sure that the Product Backlog is clear and accessible to all relevant parties.
answer2: Defining the technical specifications of Product Backlog items.
explanation2: Incorrect: Technical specifications are typically defined collaboratively with the Developers.
answer3: Ordering the Product Backlog items to maximize value.
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner prioritizes the Product Backlog items to ensure the team works on the most valuable tasks first.
answer4: Setting deadlines for Product Backlog items.
explanation4: Incorrect: The team collaborates on planning and setting expectations but does not set hard deadlines in the Product Backlog.
answer5: Delegating the management of the Product Backlog to the Developers.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner remains accountable for the Product Backlog, even with input from the Developers.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders suggest significant changes to the product. What should the Scrum Team do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team should use stakeholder feedback from the Sprint Review to update the Product Backlog, ensuring that future Sprints address the suggested changes. The Sprint Review is a working session, and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Implement the changes immediately to satisfy stakeholders.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes should be evaluated and planned for future Sprints, not made on the spot during the Review.
answer2: Discuss the feedback and update the Product Backlog to reflect the suggested changes.
explanation2: Correct: Feedback from stakeholders should be used to update the Product Backlog, guiding future work.
answer3: Ignore the feedback if it conflicts with the current Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: All feedback is valuable and should be considered for future planning.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to negotiate with stakeholders to reduce the changes.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates the process but does not negotiate scope changes on behalf of the team.

title: How can the Scrum Master help a Scrum Team struggling with low engagement during the Daily Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master can facilitate the Daily Scrum, ensuring it remains focused, interactive, and aligned with the Sprint Goal, boosting team engagement. The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Conduct one-on-one meetings instead of the Daily Scrum.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is a team event, and one-on-one meetings would not foster team collaboration.
answer2: Facilitate the Daily Scrum to keep it focused, interactive, and aligned with the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master can help by facilitating the event to make it more engaging and purposeful for the team.
answer3: Remove the Daily Scrum if the team finds it unnecessary.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is essential for inspection and adaptation and should not be removed.
answer4: Allow team members to skip the Daily Scrum if they have nothing to report.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is about team alignment, not just individual updates.

title: The Developers have identified that their Sprint Goals are often too ambitious. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions during Sprint Planning, helping the team to set realistic and achievable Sprint Goals, promoting confidence and success. The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint, providing guidance to the Developers on why they are building the Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Encourage the team to continue setting ambitious goals to drive performance.
explanation1: Incorrect: Unrealistic goals can demotivate the team if consistently missed.
answer2: Facilitate discussions during Sprint Planning to set more realistic and achievable Sprint Goals.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating Sprint Planning helps the team set achievable goals that are aligned with their capacity and capabilities.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to lower the expectations for the Sprint Goals.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Goals should be set collaboratively and reflect the team's capacity, not arbitrarily lowered.
answer4: Let the team decide on their goals without intervention to promote self-management.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should support the team in setting achievable goals through facilitation and coaching.

title: The Developers notice that their work is being frequently interrupted by external requests during the Sprint. How should they address this issue? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers should use the Daily Scrum to discuss interruptions and adapt their plan, ensuring they stay aligned with the Sprint Goal. The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ignore the external requests and focus solely on their current tasks.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring external requests without proper communication can lead to conflicts and misunderstandings.
answer2: Raise the issue during the Daily Scrum and discuss how to handle interruptions as a team.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum is the right time to discuss challenges and adapt the team’s plan to handle interruptions.
answer3: Report the interruptions to the Product Owner and let them handle it.
explanation3: Incorrect: The team should manage interruptions collaboratively, not delegate them entirely to the Product Owner.
answer4: Extend the Sprint to accommodate the additional work caused by interruptions.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed and should not be extended.

title: Which action can the Scrum Master take to help the Product Owner prioritize the Product Backlog more effectively? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master can facilitate stakeholder workshops to help the Product Owner gather feedback and align priorities, ensuring the Product Backlog is well-ordered to maximize value. The Scrum Master serves the Product Owner in several ways, including finding techniques for effective Product Backlog management. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Take over the prioritization of the Product Backlog to speed up the process.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not take over the Product Owner’s responsibilities.
answer2: Facilitate stakeholder workshops to gather feedback and clarify priorities.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating workshops helps the Product Owner align the Product Backlog with stakeholder needs and priorities.
answer3: Ignore prioritization issues unless they directly impact the Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: Prioritization is critical for guiding the team’s work and should not be ignored.
answer4: Ask the Developers to help the Product Owner prioritize items.
explanation4: Incorrect: While Developers provide input, prioritization remains the Product Owner’s responsibility.

title: A Scrum Team consistently fails to complete all items in the Sprint Backlog. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate a Retrospective to help the team understand why items are not being completed and to identify actions that can improve their future performance. The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements to be enacted during the next Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Extend the Sprint length to give the team more time to complete their work.
explanation1: Incorrect: Extending Sprints undermines the time-boxing principle of Scrum.
answer2: Facilitate a Retrospective to identify why items are not being completed and plan improvements.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective allows the team to inspect their performance and make adjustments to improve in future Sprints.
answer3: Assign fewer items to the team in the next Sprint to reduce their workload.
explanation3: Incorrect: The team should collaboratively decide how much work to take on based on their capacity.
answer4: Ignore the issue as long as the team delivers some value at the end of the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Consistently failing to complete work suggests deeper issues that need to be addressed.

title: Which two roles are most involved in ensuring the Definition of Done is understood and applied? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Developers are directly responsible for meeting the Definition of Done, with support from the Scrum Master to ensure quality standards are upheld. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Product Owner and Developers
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for prioritizing work, but the Developers ensure the Definition of Done is met.
answer2: Scrum Master and Product Owner
explanation2: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates understanding, but the Developers are responsible for applying the Definition of Done.
answer3: Developers and Scrum Master
explanation3: Correct: The Developers ensure that their work meets the Definition of Done, while the Scrum Master supports by facilitating understanding and adherence to quality standards.
answer4: Developers and Stakeholders
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide feedback but do not directly enforce the Definition of Done.
answer5: Scrum Master and Stakeholders
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholders are involved in feedback but not in maintaining the Definition of Done.

title: Which two strategies can help a Scrum Team enhance the quality of their Increments? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Regular pair programming and integrating quality metrics into the Definition of Done help Scrum Teams consistently deliver high-quality Increments. The Definition of Done helps ensure quality standards are met consistently. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Lowering the Definition of Done standards to ensure all items can be completed on time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering standards compromises the quality and value of the Increment.
answer2: Conducting regular pair programming sessions to improve code quality and knowledge sharing.
explanation2: Correct: Pair programming fosters collaboration and improves the overall quality of the work produced.
answer3: Including quality metrics in the Definition of Done to ensure specific standards are consistently met.
explanation3: Correct: Quality metrics help the team maintain focus on essential quality aspects throughout development.
answer4: Deferring testing activities to the end of the Sprint to save time during development.
explanation4: Incorrect: Delaying testing can lead to rushed work and missed quality issues.
answer5: Assigning specific team members to handle all quality-related tasks independently.
explanation5: Incorrect: Quality should be a shared responsibility among all team members.

title: A Scrum Team consistently delivers Increments that lack the expected quality. What action should the Scrum Master take? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate reviews of the Definition of Done and provide training on quality practices, helping the team meet standards consistently. The Definition of Done helps ensure quality standards are met consistently. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Product Owner to lower quality expectations for the next Sprints.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering expectations compromises the product's value and does not solve the quality issue.
answer2: Facilitate a review of the Definition of Done and provide training on quality practices to help the team meet standards consistently.
explanation2: Correct: Reviewing the Definition of Done and training the team supports quality improvements and consistent delivery.
answer3: Reassign quality assurance tasks to the most experienced Developers.
explanation3: Incorrect: Quality is a shared responsibility and should be integrated into the entire team's workflow.
answer4: Ignore the quality issues, assuming they will resolve naturally as the team gains more experience.
explanation4: Incorrect: Quality issues need proactive resolution to maintain product integrity and stakeholder trust.

title: A Scrum Team has completed a feature, but stakeholders are dissatisfied with the outcome. How should the Scrum Master handle this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to capture stakeholder feedback and adjust the Product Backlog, ensuring future work aligns with expectations. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Developers to rework the feature immediately to address stakeholder concerns.
explanation1: Incorrect: Immediate rework without proper planning can disrupt the Sprint and impact other commitments.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the stakeholders and the Product Owner to capture feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: Capturing feedback and adjusting the backlog ensures that future work aligns better with stakeholder expectations.
answer3: Ignore the dissatisfaction since the feature met the Definition of Done.
explanation3: Incorrect: Meeting the Definition of Done is necessary, but stakeholder feedback is crucial for continuous improvement.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to handle the feedback independently.
explanation4: Incorrect: Feedback should be collaboratively addressed to ensure alignment and continuous improvement.

title: During a Sprint, the Scrum Master notices that the Developers are not collaborating effectively. What action should the Scrum Master take? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should focus on coaching the team to improve their collaboration and communication practices. The Scrum Master helps everyone understand Scrum theory and practice. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Step in and reassign tasks to ensure work is completed.
explanation1: Incorrect: This contradicts the self-managing nature of the Scrum Team.
answer2: Coach the team on effective collaboration and communication practices.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team improve collaboration skills.
answer3: Report the issue to management for intervention.
explanation3: Incorrect: Management intervention disrupts the self-managing principle.
answer4: Let the team handle it themselves; it's their responsibility.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should guide the team to improve without directly intervening in their task assignments.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies that they often miss the Definition of Done. What should the Scrum Master suggest? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach the team on refining their processes to ensure they consistently meet the Definition of Done. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Lower the Definition of Done standards to make it achievable.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering quality standards is not a solution.
answer2: Coach the team on improving their processes to consistently meet the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should help the team refine their processes to meet quality standards consistently.
answer3: Remove items from the Definition of Done during the Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Adjusting the Definition of Done mid-Sprint disrupts consistency and quality.
answer4: Ignore the issue and focus on speed.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring quality compromises the overall value delivered.

title: The Developers are consistently unable to meet their Sprint commitment due to unexpected technical debt. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions that help the team identify the root causes of technical debt and find ways to address them. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Add more Developers to the team to handle the extra work.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding people can disrupt team dynamics and is not a sustainable solution.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to identify and address the root cause of the technical debt.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should help the team address the root causes of technical debt through collaboration and improvement.
answer3: Reduce the scope of the Sprint without involving the Product Owner.
explanation3: Incorrect: The scope should only be adjusted through negotiation with the Product Owner.
answer4: Ignore the issue and allow the team to handle it on their own.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master plays a key role in helping the team improve and address challenges.

title: What is the best way for the Developers to handle technical debt in a Scrum environment? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Technical debt should be made visible in the Product Backlog and addressed during Sprints as prioritized by the Product Owner, ensuring that quality remains high. The Scrum Team ensures quality by adhering to a Definition of Done that requires any technical debt to be resolved. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ignore it until it becomes critical.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring technical debt can lead to quality issues and increased maintenance costs.
answer2: Include it in the Product Backlog and address it during future Sprints.
explanation2: Correct: Technical debt should be visible and prioritized like any other backlog item.
answer3: Handle it during a special hardening Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Scrum does not support special Sprints dedicated to fixing technical debt.
answer4: Assign it to specialists outside the team.
explanation4: Incorrect: All work, including technical debt, should be managed by the Scrum Team.

title: Which Scrum value is demonstrated when a team works together to complete a challenging task despite difficulties? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Commitment is a core Scrum value demonstrated when the team dedicates themselves to achieving their goals, even when faced with difficulties. Scrum Team members commit to achieving their goals and supporting each other. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Commitment
explanation1: Correct: Commitment is shown when the team works together and perseveres through challenges to achieve their goals.
answer2: Focus
explanation2: Incorrect: Focus relates to concentrating on the work of the Sprint Goal but does not specifically address overcoming difficulties.
answer3: Openness
explanation3: Incorrect: Openness involves sharing progress and challenges but is not specifically about perseverance.
answer4: Respect
explanation4: Incorrect: Respect involves valuing each other’s contributions but is not directly about overcoming challenges together.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is solely responsible for ordering the Product Backlog to maximize value. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is the only role accountable for ordering the Product Backlog to maximize product value. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner is solely accountable for ordering the Product Backlog and ensuring it maximizes product value.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing and ordering the Product Backlog.

title: Which three activities should the Product Owner regularly engage in to maximize the value delivered by the Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Regular backlog refinement, stakeholder engagement, and collaboration with the Scrum Master help the Product Owner maximize the value delivered by the Scrum Team. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Constantly refining and prioritizing the Product Backlog based on stakeholder input.
explanation1: Correct: Continuous refinement helps ensure that the Product Backlog reflects the most current and valuable work.
answer2: Micromanaging the team’s daily tasks to ensure alignment with the Product Goal.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner should focus on backlog management, not micromanaging the team’s work.
answer3: Engaging with stakeholders to gather feedback and ensure alignment with market needs.
explanation3: Correct: Stakeholder engagement helps keep the Product Backlog aligned with external needs and expectations.
answer4: Approving every task before it is started by the Developers.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner prioritizes work but does not approve individual tasks.
answer5: Collaborating closely with the Scrum Master to address impediments that impact value delivery.
explanation5: Correct: Collaboration with the Scrum Master ensures that the team can address impediments efficiently and maintain focus on value.

title: The Scrum Master notices that the Product Owner is not engaging adequately with the Developers. What actions should the Scrum Master take? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach the Product Owner and facilitate workshops to improve communication, enhancing collaboration between the Product Owner and Developers. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team focus on creating high-value Increments that meet the Definition of Done. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Coach the Product Owner on their role and the importance of collaboration with the team.
explanation1: Correct: Coaching helps the Product Owner understand their responsibilities and improve engagement.
answer2: Facilitate workshops to improve communication between the Product Owner and Developers.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating collaboration workshops can help bridge communication gaps.
answer3: Take over the Product Owner’s responsibilities temporarily.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not take over responsibilities of other roles.
answer4: Report the issue to management for intervention.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should address the issue within the team before escalating.
answer5: Ignore the situation as it does not directly impact the Scrum Master’s duties.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master is responsible for ensuring effective team collaboration.

title: Which two actions are essential for the Product Owner to maximize the value of the product? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner maximizes value by prioritizing the Product Backlog and clearly communicating the vision and Product Goal to the Scrum Team. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assigning specific tasks to Developers during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Developers manage their own tasks; the Product Owner focuses on backlog management.
answer2: Prioritizing the Product Backlog to ensure the most valuable work is done first.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog to maximize value.
answer3: Communicating the vision and Product Goal clearly to the Scrum Team.
explanation3: Correct: Effective communication ensures the team understands what needs to be achieved.
answer4: Facilitating the Daily Scrum to keep the team focused.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates events; the Product Owner focuses on value.
answer5: Reporting team performance to stakeholders regularly.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner manages backlog transparency and prioritization, not performance reporting.

title: Which two activities are critical for the Product Owner during a Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner's key responsibilities include prioritizing the Product Backlog and collaborating with stakeholders to refine it based on feedback. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Managing the Developers' daily tasks.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Developers manage their own tasks; the Product Owner focuses on backlog management.
answer2: Ordering the Product Backlog to ensure the most valuable work is prioritized.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value by prioritizing the backlog.
answer3: Attending the Daily Scrum to track progress.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s attendance at Daily Scrums is optional, not mandatory.
answer4: Collaborating with stakeholders to refine the Product Backlog based on feedback.
explanation4: Correct: Stakeholder collaboration ensures the Product Backlog reflects the most valuable work.
answer5: Facilitating the Sprint Retrospective.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates the Sprint Retrospective, not the Product Owner.

title: Which two roles are essential during the refinement of the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Backlog refinement involves the Product Owner and Developers working together to ensure items are ready for future Sprints. The Product Owner and Developers collaborate on Product Backlog refinement as needed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Scrum Master and Developers
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not actively refine.
answer2: Product Owner and Developers
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner and Developers collaborate on refining the Product Backlog.
answer3: Scrum Master and Product Owner
explanation3: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master can facilitate, the Developers and Product Owner do the refinement.
answer4: Stakeholders and Product Owner
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide input but are not involved directly in refinement.
answer5: Developers and Stakeholders
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholders do not directly refine; they provide feedback.

title: A Developer feels overwhelmed by their workload and asks the Scrum Master for help. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate a team discussion to help the Developers self-manage their workload, ensuring the team can adapt and continue to work effectively. Developers are self-managing, meaning they internally decide who does what, when, and how. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assign some of the work to another Developer to balance the load.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Developers are self-managing and decide together how to handle their work.
answer2: Facilitate a team discussion to redistribute the work or adjust the plan.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should facilitate a discussion, allowing the team to self-manage and adapt as needed.
answer3: Take on some of the work themselves to help the Developer.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not do the work of the Developers.
answer4: Report the workload issue to the Product Owner.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should address the issue within the team rather than escalating externally.

title: A Developer is frequently taking on more work than they can handle, causing delays. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions that help the team manage their workload, improve estimation, and balance task distribution to avoid overcommitment. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Instruct the Developer to complete tasks faster to keep up with commitments.
explanation1: Incorrect: Speeding up work compromises quality and sustainability.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to help the team address workload management and improve task estimation.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master supports the team in managing their workload effectively through better estimation and planning.
answer3: Reassign the Developer’s tasks to others to balance the workload.
explanation3: Incorrect: Task reassignment is not a sustainable solution and disrupts team dynamics.
answer4: Extend the Sprint to give more time for task completion.
explanation4: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint disrupts the regular Scrum cadence.

title: A Product Owner frequently changes the priority of Product Backlog items during the Sprint. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach the Product Owner on the importance of maintaining focus during the Sprint to avoid disruptions and help the team stay aligned with the Sprint Goal. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team understand the need for clear and concise Product Backlog items. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allow the changes to keep the team focused on high-priority work.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes during the Sprint can disrupt the team’s focus and should be minimized.
answer2: Coach the Product Owner on the importance of maintaining a stable Sprint Backlog during the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should coach the Product Owner to minimize changes that could affect team focus and the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Ask the team to ignore the Product Owner’s changes.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should not encourage ignoring any role's input but should facilitate proper communication.
answer4: Extend the Sprint to accommodate the changes.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed and should not be extended.

title: A Scrum Team finds it difficult to implement new technologies due to a lack of specific expertise. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate training and learning opportunities to help the team build the skills needed to adopt new technologies, supporting continuous improvement. The Scrum Team is cross-functional, meaning the members have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assign the tasks requiring new technology to the most experienced Developers.
explanation1: Incorrect: Assigning tasks based solely on experience can create bottlenecks and does not address the skill gap.
answer2: Facilitate training sessions or pair programming opportunities to build the necessary skills within the team.
explanation2: Correct: Providing learning opportunities helps the team gain the skills needed to adopt new technologies effectively.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to remove all items requiring new technologies from the backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: Avoiding technological advancements limits the team’s growth and adaptability.
answer4: Outsource the tasks to external experts temporarily.
explanation4: Incorrect: Outsourcing disrupts team dynamics and does not help the team develop needed skills internally.

title: A Scrum Team is struggling with maintaining focus during their Sprints due to frequent interruptions. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team identify and manage interruptions, enabling them to maintain focus on the Sprint Goal. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Remind the team to ignore external requests until the Sprint is over.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring external requests without proper communication may cause misalignment with stakeholders.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to identify the source of interruptions and establish boundaries.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team manage interruptions and maintain focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Adjust the Sprint Backlog to accommodate the interruptions.
explanation3: Incorrect: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog mid-Sprint disrupts the team’s focus and planning.
answer4: Escalate the issue to upper management to prevent further interruptions.
explanation4: Incorrect: The issue should be managed within the Scrum Team through improved communication and processes.

title: During a Sprint, a Developer identifies a technical impediment that could delay the Sprint Goal. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team identify and resolve impediments, ensuring progress toward the Sprint Goal. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team remove impediments to the team’s progress. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Developer to work extra hours to resolve the issue.
explanation1: Incorrect: Encouraging overwork is not a sustainable or effective solution.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the team to explore possible solutions and remove the impediment.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team address impediments and find collaborative solutions.
answer3: Escalate the problem to management for a quick fix.
explanation3: Incorrect: Issues should be handled within the Scrum Team whenever possible.
answer4: Ignore the impediment and focus on the Sprint Goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring impediments can jeopardize the Sprint Goal.

title: During a Sprint, a team member consistently misses Daily Scrums, citing work overload. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should address attendance issues directly to ensure the team maintains regular communication and alignment during Daily Scrums. The Daily Scrum is a key event for self-management and collaboration. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ignore the absences if the work is being completed on time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Regular attendance is essential for team alignment and communication.
answer2: Discuss with the team member privately to understand the issue and stress the importance of participation.
explanation2: Correct: Addressing the issue directly helps the team member understand their role in team collaboration.
answer3: Reassign the team member’s tasks to others to reduce their workload.
explanation3: Incorrect: Redistributing work may temporarily relieve the burden but doesn’t address the root cause of missed meetings.
answer4: Report the issue to management for further action.
explanation4: Incorrect: Handling such issues internally helps maintain trust and team cohesion.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers express concerns about not having all the required skills to complete a critical task. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team address skill gaps through collaboration and knowledge sharing, ensuring the Sprint Goal is achievable. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assign the task to the most skilled Developer to ensure it's completed.
explanation1: Incorrect: Task assignment is not the role of the Scrum Master; the team should self-organize to address skill gaps.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on how the team can share knowledge or find alternative ways to complete the task.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team find collaborative solutions to skill gaps.
answer3: Ignore the concern, assuming the team will figure it out.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring skill gaps can lead to incomplete work and missed Sprint Goals.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to adjust the Sprint Backlog to remove the task.
explanation4: Incorrect: Adjusting the backlog should be a last resort; first, the team should explore ways to complete the task.

title: True or False: The Product Backlog should be kept static and only updated at the end of each Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog is continuously updated to reflect the current state of requirements, ensuring it remains relevant and aligned with stakeholder needs. The Product Backlog is a dynamic, ordered list that is regularly refined to maximize value. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog is dynamic and should be updated regularly to reflect new insights and feedback.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Backlog is a living document that evolves as new information becomes available, ensuring it reflects the latest priorities and requirements.

title: Which three best practices can help a Scrum Team maintain a healthy Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maintaining a healthy Product Backlog involves regular refinement, stakeholder collaboration, and updating items based on feedback. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Regularly refining items to ensure they are clear and actionable.
explanation1: Correct: Refinement keeps the Product Backlog up to date and ensures items are ready for future Sprints.
answer2: Assigning tasks to specific Developers during refinement sessions.
explanation2: Incorrect: Tasks are not assigned during refinement; the focus is on clarifying and estimating items.
answer3: Collaborating with stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust priorities.
explanation3: Correct: Stakeholder input helps keep the Product Backlog aligned with current needs and priorities.
answer4: Documenting detailed specifications for every Product Backlog item.
explanation4: Incorrect: Detailed documentation is not necessary; clarity and alignment with the Product Goal are more important.
answer5: Using feedback from completed Sprints to update the Product Backlog.
explanation5: Correct: Feedback helps the Product Owner adjust priorities and refine items to better meet stakeholder needs.

title: Which three elements are critical to the Sprint Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog includes the selected Product Backlog items, the Sprint Goal, and the plan for achieving the Sprint Goal. The Sprint Backlog is a highly visible, real-time picture of the work that the Developers plan to accomplish. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: The selected Product Backlog items for the Sprint.
explanation1: Correct: These items represent the work planned for the Sprint.
answer2: A detailed list of tasks for each team member.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog does not contain task lists; it’s a plan by the Developers.
answer3: The Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Correct: The Sprint Goal provides direction and focus for the Sprint.
answer4: The plan for how the Developers will work together to achieve the Sprint Goal.
explanation4: Correct: This plan helps guide the Developers in completing the work needed for the Sprint.
answer5: A review of completed work from the last Sprint.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog focuses on the current Sprint, not past work.

title: Which three elements should be included in the Sprint Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog includes the selected Product Backlog items, the Sprint Goal, and the plan for achieving that goal. The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: The Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint.
explanation1: Correct: These items represent the work that the team plans to complete during the Sprint.
answer2: The Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal provides focus and guidance for the team’s work during the Sprint.
answer3: The completed Increment from the previous Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment reflects completed work and is not part of the Sprint Backlog.
answer4: The plan for how the team will achieve the Sprint Goal.
explanation4: Correct: The team’s plan outlines how they will complete the selected Product Backlog items.
answer5: The Product Owner’s approval of each task.
explanation5: Incorrect: Approval processes are not part of the Sprint Backlog; it focuses on the team’s work plan and goals.

title: Which two key responsibilities does the Product Owner have during backlog refinement? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner collaborates with the Developers to refine and prioritize Product Backlog items, ensuring that the backlog is clear, actionable, and aligned with stakeholder needs. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Setting estimates for Product Backlog items to guide planning decisions.
explanation1: Incorrect: Estimation is a responsibility of the Developers, not the Product Owner.
answer2: Collaborating with Developers to clarify and refine items, ensuring they are ready for future Sprints.
explanation2: Correct: Collaboration helps ensure that backlog items are clear, actionable, and aligned with current priorities.
answer3: Prioritizing items based on stakeholder feedback, market conditions, and product strategy.
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for ensuring that the backlog reflects the latest priorities and strategy.
answer4: Handling all refinement sessions independently to maintain control over the Product Backlog.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement should be a collaborative effort, not managed by the Product Owner alone.
answer5: Delegating refinement tasks to team members to speed up the process.
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement is best done collaboratively to ensure shared understanding and alignment.

title: Which two roles work together most closely to ensure the Product Backlog reflects the current priorities? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner collaborates closely with the Developers and receives support from the Scrum Master to ensure the Product Backlog is well managed and prioritized. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Scrum Master and Product Owner
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner manages the Product Backlog with support from the Scrum Master in facilitating discussions and refinement.
answer2: Developers and Stakeholders
explanation2: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide feedback, but the Developers work directly with the Product Owner on backlog items.
answer3: Product Owner and Developers
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner collaborates with the Developers to refine and prioritize items based on the latest needs and insights.
answer4: Scrum Master and Stakeholders
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide input, but managing the backlog is not a direct responsibility of the Scrum Master.
answer5: Product Owner and Stakeholders
explanation5: Incorrect: While stakeholders influence priorities, the Product Owner manages the Product Backlog.

title: A Scrum Team is experiencing repeated issues with unclear requirements during Sprints. What action should the Scrum Master take? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate refinement sessions to ensure that Product Backlog items are clear and understood, minimizing issues during Sprints. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Instruct the Developers to proceed based on their best guess.
explanation1: Incorrect: Assumptions without clarification can lead to errors and misalignment.
answer2: Facilitate a backlog refinement session to improve the clarity of Product Backlog items.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement helps ensure that requirements are clear and well understood before Sprints.
answer3: Ignore the issue as part of the natural challenges of development.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring the issue can lead to ongoing inefficiencies and reduced product quality.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to simplify requirements to avoid confusion.
explanation4: Incorrect: Simplification is not always the solution; clarity and thorough understanding are key.

title: What is the main purpose of refining Product Backlog items during a Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The main purpose of refining Product Backlog items is to ensure they are clear, well-understood, and ready for selection in future Sprints. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To assign tasks to specific Developers before the next Sprint Planning.
explanation1: Incorrect: Refinement focuses on clarifying items, not assigning tasks.
answer2: To ensure that items are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement helps the team prepare work that can be easily understood and executed in upcoming Sprints.
answer3: To decide which items will be worked on in the current Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Sprint Planning, not refinement, determines what will be worked on in the current Sprint.
answer4: To estimate the time required for each task in the Product Backlog.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement is about understanding and prioritizing items, not detailed task time estimation.

title: What is the primary function of the Definition of Ready in Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Ready sets the criteria that Product Backlog items must meet to be considered ready for inclusion in a Sprint, ensuring clarity and actionability. Product Backlog items that can be considered for selection in a Sprint should meet the Definition of Ready. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To ensure that all Product Backlog items are fully detailed before being selected for a Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: While detail is important, the Definition of Ready focuses on readiness for work, not exhaustive detailing.
answer2: To set criteria that Product Backlog items must meet before being accepted into a Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Ready ensures that items are clear, actionable, and ready for inclusion in a Sprint.
answer3: To validate that completed work meets all quality standards.
explanation3: Incorrect: This is the purpose of the Definition of Done, not the Definition of Ready.
answer4: To guarantee that the Sprint Goal will be achieved.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Ready helps prepare work for Sprints but does not guarantee goal achievement.

title: What is the primary role of the Product Backlog in Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog is an ordered list of all work needed for the product, maintained by the Product Owner to maximize value. The Product Backlog is an ordered list of everything that is known to be needed in the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To assign tasks to Developers during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog does not assign tasks; it lists work needed for the product.
answer2: To provide an ordered list of all work needed for the product, managed by the Product Owner.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Backlog is managed by the Product Owner to ensure it reflects the most valuable work.
answer3: To track the team’s performance over time.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Backlog focuses on future work, not performance tracking.
answer4: To ensure all team members have an equal workload.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Backlog prioritizes work based on value, not equal distribution of tasks.

title: True or False: During the Daily Scrum, each Developer must provide an update on their progress toward the Sprint Goal. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum focuses on how each Developer’s progress contributes to achieving the Sprint Goal and planning the next steps. The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Daily Scrum focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal and how to plan the next 24 hours.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is about inspecting progress and adapting plans to meet the Sprint Goal.

title: True or False: The Sprint Planning event is critical for setting the direction of the Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Sprint Planning sets the Sprint Goal and defines the work that the Developers will undertake, providing direction for the Sprint. The purpose of Sprint Planning is to define what can be delivered in the Sprint and how that work will be achieved. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: Sprint Planning defines what can be done during the Sprint and sets the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Incorrect: Sprint Planning is essential for setting the Sprint’s direction and planning the work.

title: Which three elements are essential to a successful Sprint Review? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Engaging stakeholders, inspecting the Product Backlog, and adapting it based on feedback are key elements of a successful Sprint Review. The Sprint Review is a working session, and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Presenting the Increment to stakeholders as a formal product release.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is a feedback session, not a formal release event.
answer2: Engaging stakeholders in a discussion about what was accomplished and how it aligns with the Product Goal.
explanation2: Correct: Stakeholder engagement helps ensure the product aligns with market needs and expectations.
answer3: Inspecting the Product Backlog and adapting it based on feedback received during the Review.
explanation3: Correct: Adaptation of the Product Backlog ensures it reflects the latest feedback and priorities.
answer4: Focusing solely on the positive aspects of the Increment to boost team morale.
explanation4: Incorrect: Constructive feedback, including areas for improvement, is essential for product growth.
answer5: Planning the next Sprint in detail to immediately incorporate feedback.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is not for detailed planning but for feedback and adaptation.

title: Which two actions are essential for the Scrum Master to facilitate an effective Sprint Retrospective? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate an inclusive and structured Sprint Retrospective to help the team identify actionable improvements. The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ensure every team member has an equal opportunity to speak.
explanation1: Correct: Equal participation helps gather diverse insights and fosters a collaborative environment.
answer2: Assign specific actions to team members for the next Sprint.
explanation2: Incorrect: Actions should be agreed upon by the team, not assigned by the Scrum Master.
answer3: Use facilitation techniques to keep the discussion focused and constructive.
explanation3: Correct: Effective facilitation helps the team stay on topic and generate valuable outcomes.
answer4: Focus only on the negative aspects to drive improvement.
explanation4: Incorrect: A balanced approach helps the team reflect on both successes and areas for improvement.
answer5: Schedule the Retrospective at the team’s convenience to ensure attendance.
explanation5: Incorrect: Retrospectives should be time-boxed and occur regularly to maintain momentum.

title: Which two practices can help prevent common anti-patterns in Sprint Planning? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Fully refined Product Backlog items and a focus on the Sprint Goal help prevent common anti-patterns in Sprint Planning, ensuring a productive and aligned planning session. Sprint Planning sets the direction of the Sprint by defining the Sprint Goal and selecting work to achieve it. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ensuring all Product Backlog items are fully refined before the Sprint Planning session.
explanation1: Correct: Fully refined items help ensure that the team can accurately plan their work.
answer2: Allowing the Scrum Master to assign tasks to team members.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates, but task assignment is done by the Developers themselves.
answer3: Keeping the focus on the Sprint Goal and the work needed to achieve it.
explanation3: Correct: A focused approach helps prevent distractions and keeps planning on track.
answer4: Skipping the discussion of the Sprint Goal to save time.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal provides direction and purpose for the Sprint.
answer5: Allowing stakeholders to participate actively in task estimation.
explanation5: Incorrect: Task estimation is a responsibility of the Scrum Team, not stakeholders.

title: A Scrum Team has trouble maintaining a steady velocity due to frequent changes in team composition. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate Retrospectives that focus on adapting to changes in team composition, helping the team find ways to maintain stability and a consistent work rhythm. The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements to be enacted during the next Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Encourage the team to ignore velocity as a metric until the team stabilizes.
explanation1: Incorrect: While velocity may fluctuate, it remains a valuable tool for understanding team performance and planning.
answer2: Facilitate Retrospectives focused on adapting to changes and finding ways to stabilize the team’s working rhythm.
explanation2: Correct: Retrospectives provide opportunities for the team to reflect on challenges and adapt their processes to maintain stability.
answer3: Assign tasks based on team members’ strengths to maximize output regardless of team changes.
explanation3: Incorrect: Task assignment should be managed collectively to promote team collaboration and learning.
answer4: Escalate the issue to management to prevent further changes in team composition.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should first help the team adapt to changes before considering escalation.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers are unsure about the complexity of a new feature. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers should break down complex features into smaller tasks, making them easier to estimate and commit to, ensuring they can meet the Sprint Goal. Product Backlog items that can be done by the Developers within one Sprint are deemed ready for selection in Sprint Planning. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Commit to the feature regardless of uncertainty.
explanation1: Incorrect: Committing to work with high uncertainty can jeopardize the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Break down the feature into smaller, manageable tasks and commit to what they understand.
explanation2: Correct: Breaking down complex items into smaller, clearer tasks helps the team commit with confidence.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to remove the feature entirely.
explanation3: Incorrect: The feature should be refined, not removed, if it is of value.
